newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-LME to hold talks on regulatory changes soon.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-LME to hold talks on regulatory changes soon.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) will meet the Securities Investment Board (SIB) authority next week to discuss regulatory changes in the wake of the Sumitomo Corp copper trading scandal, LME chief executive David King said on Wednesday.

The discussions would focus on the outcome of a review by the SIB of 3,500 users of the exchange over how the LME provided price transparancies, operated its vast warehousing system and other issues, King said in a speech to the Australian Metals Conference here. "There will not, we believe, be any fundamental changes," King said.
King said the majority of the users of the LME were happy with the current cash clearing system.
He said the LME would explore ways to provide more public information to improve price transparencies.
In warehousing, King said the LME needed to "strike a balance" over the operation of its 380 warehouses.
"The LME cannot possibly be the world's policeman of physical metal," King said.
Turnover on the LME has grown 700 percent in the last eight years and the LME represents the world's largest and most liquid nonferrous base metals market, King said.
"We have 95 percent of the world's futures copper trading business and nearly 100 percent of the business in respect of the other LME metals traded, King said.
The LME trades copper, lead, nickel, zinc, aluminium tin and aluminium alloy.

King said the arrest of Sumitomo's former top trader Yasuo Hamanaka for alleged forgery on October 22 was the result of an investigation initiated by the LME into over-the-counter, on-exchange and physical trading of copper.
